Title: Show Statistics (ver. 12.1)
Content: Feature Overview You can check various information related to the garment through the 'Show Statistics' Steps Follow the indicated guideline below to open 'Show Statistics'. Location Main Menu Display Environment Show Statistics View Options icon (3D Window) Environment Display Show Statistics End Result Information related to the garment will be displayed at the left bottom corner of the 3D Window. Please refer to the table below for the information items. Vertices The number of the vertices Edges The number of the edges Triangles The number of the triangular meshes Faces The number of the entire faces Patterns The number of the pattern pieces Trims The number of the trims Sewings The number of the Seam Line Pair Group CPUs The number of the activated CPU Fps Frames per Second, Simulation speed. F Garment, gravity time I Linear system time P Garment-garment proximity time S Garment-garment collision time O Avatar skinning time SK Avatar skinning + Joint animation time E Time excluding clothing simulation and avatar skinning in the overall simulation. R Rendering time. UI UI update time. T Simulation + Rendering + UI update time.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a comprehensive guide on how to access and interpret garment-related statistics within a 3D simulation environment.

Title: Garment Fit Maps
Content: Objective Utilize four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to check 3D Gament's fit. Location 3D Window Hover the Mouse Over the 5th Icon Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window Hover the Mouse Over the 5th Icon Four Garment Fit Maps appear. Refer to the table below and select the desired view icon. Icon Description Stress Map (Below ver. 12) External stress causing garment distortion per area of the fabric appears in the range of color and numbers. Stress Map appears in a total of eight colors: Red indicates the strongest stress (100kPa) while blue indicates zero distortion (0.00kPa). Other numbers in between are expressed as gradation of two colors. Strain Map Garment's distortion rate due to external stress appears in percentage. Stain Map appears in a total of eight colors: Red indicates a 120% of distortion rate while blue indicates 100% (no distortion). Numbers in between are expressed as gradation of two colors. Fit Map (Below ver. 12) Fip Map shows the tightness of the 3D Garment. Can't Wear appears in red indicating not wearable area. Very Tight appears in orange indicating a very tight area. Tight appears in yellow indicating a slightly tight area. Show Pressure Points Show or hide contact points between 3D Garment and Avatar. Based on the selected icon, Stress Map, Strain Map, Fit Map, or Pressure Points appear on the 3D Garment.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a guide for utilizing four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to assess the fit and stress levels of a 3D garment.

Title: Wind Controller Setting
Content: Objective Adjust and apply wind effect to create fluttering effect on garment in the 3D window. Location Main Menu Display Show Wind Controller Operation Activate Wind Effect 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Environment Show Wind Controller Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2. Click the Wind Controller. Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Wind Toggle on (Check Box) at Activate. It is now being activated (Toggled On) and becomes in blue color. 4. Click Simulation. The Wind Effect is now being activated in the 3D window. Wind Direction Setting 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Show Wind Controller Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2. Click the Wind Controller. Wind Controller Gizmo activates. 3. Use the Gizmo to set direction and location of the wind. 4. Click Simulation. The Wind Effect is now being activated as adjusted in the 3D window. Wind Properties Setting 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Show Wind Controller Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2. Click the Wind Controller. Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Adjust the default values at Property Editor according to the needs. Name Changes name of the wind according to the user preference. Wind Activate Sets the activation status of the wind. Type Sets the type of the wind. Spherical: The wind blows in spherical shape, in every direction starting from the Wind Controller. Planar: The wind blows only from the designated direction, regardless of the Wind Controller's location. Strength Sets the intensity of the wind. The higher the value, the stronger the wind. Decay [0~100] Sets the range of the wind. The wind draws an arc and blows weaker according to the set value of wind intensity. If the value is "0", it blows in a straight line endlessly. Frequency (sec) Sets the cycle of the wind. The wind repeatably blows weaker and stronger in interval of set value of seconds. If the value is "0", it blows regularly. Turbulence [0~100] Sets the turbulence of wind intensity. The higher the value, the more irregular the wind intensity.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for adjusting and applying wind effects to create a realistic fluttering motion on garments within a 3D environment.

Title: 2D Pattern Window Ruler (Ver. 2024.1)
Content: Objective Place 2D elements or create pattern using Ruler and Guidelines in 2D Window. Location 2D Window 2D Information Show Ruler 2D Window 2D Information Show Guideline Operation Show/Hide Ruler and Settings 1. In the 2D window, click 2D Information Show Ruler Ruler appears in 2D window. 2. Right click on Ruler to change the unit (Inch, Centimeter, Millimeter). 3. Click and drag the cross point on the top left of the tape measure to change the origin point. Note: The ruler is automatically scaled according to the mouse wheel up and down. Set Ruler Origin Point 1. Click and drag at the empty square in the upper left corner of the ruler. 2. When dragged, a white crosshair will be displayed. 3. When the mouse click is released, the origin point is set to the crosshair position. Note: To re-initialize the origin point: double-click or right-click the empty square in the upper left corner of the ruler. Create, Move and Show/Hide Guidelines 1. Turn on Show Ruler. 2. Click and drag either the vertical or the horizontal ruler. A guideline is created. 3. Click and drag the created guideline to move it. The guide line is moved. 4. In the 2D window, click 2D Information Show Guideline The guide display is toggled on or off. Note: A guideline adjacent to pattern points will snap to the point. Conversely, a pattern point will snap to the adjacent guideline. If Show Guideline is disabled, it will automatically set to activate when a new guideline is created. Show Guideline can operate independently from Show Ruler. (Even if Show Ruler is turned off, Show Guideline is maintained.) Hold down Ctrl key on the keyboard and drag at either the vertical or the horizontal ruler to create a guideline at the opposite axis. Set Guideline Options Right Click Options Offset Guideline Create a new guideline at regular intervals (in the Offset internal Line popup window) based on the selected guideline. Lock Guideline Lock the selected guideline. Note: Right click on a locked guideline to find the option for Unlock Guideline to unlock selected guideline. Right-Click on empty space in the 2D window, in the popup window you can select Lock All Guidelines or Unlock All Guidelines to lock or unlock all the guidelines. Delete Guideline Delete the selected guideline. Note: Hold Shift key on keyboard to select multiple guidelines, you can delete selected guidelines by executing Delete Guideline. Delete All Guidelines Delete all guidelines in the 2D window. Offset Guideline Options Number of Offsets Number of Guidelines to be created Distance Set how to give a distance value. All: Apply the same distance value to all Guidelines Individual: Apply different distance values to each guideline When set to individual, new options appears (ex: #1, #2) which allows number input for each individual guideline Offset from Offset reference point. From: Previous line : Apply distance value from the previous Guideline (gray ghost lines). selected line : Apply distance value from selected Original Guideline. Reverse Direction Create in the opposite direction from the current direction. Both Sides Create in both directions based on the Original Guideline. End Result Add ruler and ruler guidelines to 2D window.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for using rulers and guidelines in the 2D window to accurately place elements and create patterns.

Title: Show 2D Measurements
Content: Objective Show or hide 2D measurements on 2D Patterns (ver2.5.0). Note: All 2D measurements are created based on the Internal Shapes/Lines drawn on Patterns. All 2D measurements are deactivated by default. In order to activate them, please navigate to the Property Editor 2D Measurements. Then, choose either the To Center or the To Outline option to expand each option's child menu. Toggle on following options to activate the 2D measurements. When you choose To Center, Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the center of the Internal Shapes/Lines. On the other hand, when you choose To Outline, Marvelous Designer calculates the distances from the Pattern outline to the outline of the Internal Shapes/Lines. Title: Gizmo Axis Setting
Content: Objective There are three different Gizmo types in Marvelous Designer. Select and utilize it as needed. Location Main Menu Preferences Gizmo 3D Window Right-click (on the 3D window) Gizmo Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Preferences Gizmo 3D Window Right-click (on the 3D window) Gizmo 2. Select a desired Gizmo. 3. Select an object with Select/Move Tool. The chosen type of Gizmo appears. 4. Click the axis of the Gizmo Drag it to the desired location. The chosen object moves along with the Gizmo. Screen Coordinate Gizmo Screen Coordinate Gizmo is based on the camera axis. Change the camera view in order to change the gizmo axis. Selected object moves along with the camera axis. Local Coordinate Gizmo Local Coordinate Gizmo axis is based on following the native direction of an object. Mainly usable when designing poses from the avatar's X-ray joint points. Selected object moves to native direction of an object. World Coordinate Gizmo World Coordinate Gizmo is based on 3D space regardless of screens or objects. Selected object moves based on 3D space regardless of screens or objects.
ContentDescription: Discover how to effectively select and utilize the three types of Gizmos in Marvelous Designer to enhance your 3D design experience.
